brief: Futures opened lower Monday after Trump rejected Iran's weekend proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, sending Brent up 4% and compounding a US 10-year yield already at 5.22%, up for a seventh straight month, the longest such streak in 50 years. GS argues this rate backdrop makes shorting Non-Profitable Tech compelling given its 20+ point outperformance over the past year. In TMT, Asia's AI-linked names fell (Hynix, Samsung -5%) even as Meta's Muse kept the domestic AI momentum trade alive, extending NDX's win streak to a new high, though GS's Callahan flags reserved optimism: sentiment is firmly negative and market breadth is at its lowest since the Dot-Com Bubble, with the median S&P stock 16% off its high even as AI strength holds the headline index up. Institutional and CTA futures positioning has been trimmed from record longs, which GS says lowers the risk of further systematic selling. PCE, ISM and payrolls this week are the next tests.
